qs.q: Mean temperatures above 21 °C in the final month of ripening tend to…
o: make acidity fall rapidly and pH rise
qs.e: Heat speeds up the respiration of malic acid. Methoxypyrazines, by contrast, fall with warmth, and anthocyanins form best between about 15 and 25 °C.

qs.q: What characterises precision viticulture?
o: Dividing the vineyard into zones using data (images, sensors) and managing them differently
Harvesting the whole vineyard in one day
qs.e: Vigour maps and sensors show variation within a block: each zone can be irrigated, fed, sprayed or harvested separately, reducing waste and improving uniformity.

qs.q: Which statement about SO₂ is correct?
o: It is antioxidant and antimicrobial, and yeasts produce a little themselves
It must be labelled only above 100 mg/L
Limits are higher for reds than whites
It is banned in EU organic wines
qs.e: Fermentation produces up to about 10 mg/L. It is labelled above 10 mg/L; reds have lower limits (tannins protect them); EU organic wine allows reduced doses, while US 'organic' wine has none added.

qs.q: Which fining agent removes the proteins that cause haze in whites?
qs.e: Bentonite is a negatively charged clay that binds the positively charged proteins. Egg white acts on tannins, PVPP on bitter phenolics, carbon on colour and odours.

qs.q: Which extraction technique is most typical of an inexpensive, ready-to-drink red?
qs.e: Heat and rotation extract colour and fruit very quickly with little hard tannin: tanks are freed early, costs are low, the wine is soft and ready.

qs.q: Which ISO standard covers environmental management?
qs.e: ISO 9001: quality; ISO 22000: food safety; ISO 14001: environment. (ISO 3591 is the standard tasting glass.)

qs.q: What margin does a specialist wine retailer usually look for?
qs.e: Smaller volumes, advice, skilled staff and stock-holding justify higher margins than a supermarket's.

qs.q: Why does a quality producer seek listings in fine-dining restaurants?
o: For visibility and prestige, which support the brand and sales elsewhere
Because that is where the largest volumes sell
qs.e: Volumes are small and mark-ups high, but presence on prestigious lists builds credibility, introduces the wine to influential customers and supports the price.

qs.q: What are the five Ps of the marketing mix used here?
qs.e: To the classic four Ps (product, price, place, promotion) People is added: those who sell and tell the wine's story.

qs.q: What does semi-carbonic maceration give a Beaujolais?
o: Colour with little tannin and kirsch and banana aromas
qs.e: 4–5 days on skins for Beaujolais and Beaujolais-Villages.

qs.q: What share of Languedoc wine is AOC?
qs.e: Nearly 70% is IGP; the rest is wine without a geographical indication.

qs.q: Why is Nebbiolo pruned with more buds?
o: The first few buds on the cane are infertile
To shield the bunches from hail
qs.e: Single Guyot is the commonest training and makes mechanical trimming easier. Nebbiolo buds early, not late.

qs.q: Why is modern Grillo made protectively?
o: It is very prone to botrytis
qs.e: Unlike many wines of the past and Marsala; over-exposed bunches lose aroma.

qs.q: How do Jumilla's vines find water with only 250–300 mm of rain?
o: Sandy soils over limestone retain groundwater
qs.e: Many vineyards are unirrigated; Monastrell tolerates drought and heat.

qs.q: Why does Baden suit Spätburgunder?
o: It is the warmest, sunniest region, further south and in the Vosges rain shadow
It has the most continental climate
qs.e: Kaiserstuhl gives the fullest; Ortenau, Tuniberg and Breisgau the most delicate. The most continental climate is Franken's.

qs.q: How is Santorini Vinsanto made?
o: Late-picked grapes sun-dried for up to two weeks, at least two years in oak
qs.e: Often in part-filled casks for oxidation: raisin, coffee, chocolate; at least 51% Assyrtiko.

qs.q: How do Lake Ontario and the Niagara Escarpment help the vineyards?
o: They drive air circulation that warms in winter, cools in summer and reduces frost and disease
They make winter protection unnecessary everywhere
qs.e: The deep lake warms and cools slowly; the escarpment also shelters from cold south-westerly winds.

qs.q: What makes Hemel-en-Aarde suited to Pinot Noir and Chardonnay?
o: Cooling Atlantic winds, north-facing aspects and clay-rich soils
qs.e: Clay reaches 55% in parts; in the southern hemisphere north-facing aspects help ripening in a cool area.

qs.q: Why are vines buried in winter in much of China?
o: To survive the cold and, above all, winter aridity: buried vines retain more water
qs.e: They are usually buried in November and dug out in March–April; the work adds 20–30% to costs.

qs.q: Who owns most of the vineyards in Champagne?
qs.e: More than 15,000 growers own about 90% of the vineyards; the houses have 10% but make 73% of sales.

qs.q: Why was the Prosecco grape renamed Glera in 2009?
o: To reserve the name Prosecco for defined areas
Because it was found to be a different variety
To separate sparkling from still wine
To comply with a labelling rule for aromatic varieties
qs.e: A grape name can be used anywhere; a protected place name cannot.

qs.q: Which term correctly describes the mousse of a sparkling wine on the palate?
qs.e: Mousse is described as delicate, creamy or aggressive.

qs.q: To what strength is a wine for biological ageing fortified?
qs.e: Above 15.5% flor struggles; at 17% it cannot survive.

qs.q: Why are vines trained on pergolas (latadas) in Madeira?
o: To let air circulate and reduce disease in a humid climate
qs.e: The pergola also leaves room for other crops, important with holdings of 0.3 hectares on average.

qs.q: Which aromas indicate biological ageing?
qs.e: They come from acetaldehyde and the autolysis of flor.
